events.title: Independence and Partition
events.what_happened: British India gained independence on 15 August 1947 and was simultaneously partitioned into India and Pakistan, triggering mass migration and communal violence.
events.why_it_happened: Decades of independence movement (Indian National Congress, Muslim League) combined with British withdrawal after WWII; the League's demand for a separate Muslim-majority state led to Partition alongside independence.
events.consequences: Formation of two independent states; large-scale population displacement and violence; the unresolved status of princely states, including Kashmir, set up future India-Pakistan disputes.
events.long_term_significance: Founding event of the modern Indian state and the root of the India-Pakistan rivalry that continues today.

events.title: Constitution comes into force
events.what_happened: India's Constitution took effect on 26 January 1950, establishing India as a sovereign democratic republic.
events.why_it_happened: The Constituent Assembly, formed after independence, drafted a founding document establishing a parliamentary democracy, federal structure, and fundamental rights.
events.consequences: Established the parliamentary system, federal structure, and fundamental rights framework still in use today.
events.long_term_significance: Basic governing framework of the Indian state.

events.title: Sino-Indian War
events.what_happened: China and India fought a brief border war over disputed Himalayan territory (Aksai Chin and the eastern sector/NEFA), which India lost militarily.
events.why_it_happened: Unresolved and undemarcated colonial-era border (the McMahon Line dispute), competing claims following China's annexation of Tibet, and breakdown of the earlier 'Hindi-Chini bhai-bhai' diplomatic period.
events.consequences: Indian military setback, loss of Aksai Chin territory to Chinese control, and a fundamental reorientation of Indian defence policy toward military modernisation.
events.long_term_significance: Root cause of the still-unresolved Line of Actual Control dispute at the heart of the modern India-China rivalry.

events.title: Bangladesh Liberation War
events.what_happened: India intervened militarily in support of Bengali nationalists in East Pakistan, resulting in a decisive Indian/Bangladeshi victory and the creation of independent Bangladesh.
events.why_it_happened: Political repression and military crackdown by the Pakistani state against the Bengali population in East Pakistan following the 1970 election, combined with a large refugee influx into India.
events.consequences: Creation of Bangladesh as an independent state; Pakistan's military defeat and loss of its eastern wing.
events.long_term_significance: Reshaped South Asia's map and cemented India as the region's dominant military power; a foundational reference point in India-Pakistan and India-Bangladesh relations.

events.title: Economic liberalisation
events.what_happened: Facing a severe balance-of-payments crisis, India undertook major economic reforms, dismantling much of its licence-permit-raj system and opening to foreign trade and investment.
events.why_it_happened: A foreign exchange reserves crisis (partly triggered by the 1990-91 Gulf War oil price shock) forced the government to seek IMF assistance conditioned on structural reform.
events.consequences: Opened India's economy to global trade and investment, setting off three decades of accelerated economic growth.
events.long_term_significance: Turning point that shaped India's modern economic trajectory and its integration into the global economy.

events.title: Pokhran-II nuclear tests
events.what_happened: India conducted a series of nuclear weapons tests, declaring itself a nuclear weapons state.
events.why_it_happened: Longstanding security concerns following the 1962 and 1971 wars and China's earlier nuclearisation, combined with a strategic decision under the BJP-led government to formalise India's nuclear deterrent.
events.consequences: International sanctions in the immediate aftermath; Pakistan conducted its own nuclear tests shortly after.
events.long_term_significance: Established India's declared nuclear deterrent, a central pillar of its strategic posture today.

events.title: Kargil War
events.what_happened: Pakistani forces and militants occupied high-altitude positions on the Indian side of the Line of Control in Kargil; India fought a limited but intense conflict to reclaim the territory.
events.why_it_happened: Pakistani military intrusion across the LoC, following the thaw of the Lahore Declaration talks earlier that year.
events.consequences: India recaptured the occupied positions; the conflict damaged Pakistan's international standing and contributed to Musharraf's later coup.
events.long_term_significance: First open military conflict between two declared nuclear powers, reinforcing the risks of India-Pakistan escalation.

events.title: India-US Civil Nuclear Agreement
events.what_happened: The US and India concluded a civil nuclear cooperation agreement, ending India's nuclear isolation despite it not being a signatory to the Non-Proliferation Treaty.
events.why_it_happened: Both countries sought a strategic partnership; the US saw India as a long-term Indo-Pacific partner and was willing to make an exception to non-proliferation norms.
events.consequences: Opened the door for India to access global civil nuclear trade and marked a significant deepening of the India-US strategic relationship.
events.long_term_significance: Foundational moment in the modern India-US strategic partnership.

events.title: Doklam standoff
events.what_happened: Indian and Chinese troops faced off for over two months near the Doklam plateau, a disputed area between China and Bhutan, after Indian forces intervened to stop Chinese road construction.
events.why_it_happened: China's road-building in territory claimed by Bhutan (an Indian security partner) was seen by India as altering the status quo near a strategically sensitive tri-junction near India's 'Chicken's Neck' corridor.
events.consequences: Resolved through diplomatic disengagement without major escalation.
events.long_term_significance: Signalled India's willingness to directly confront Chinese infrastructure assertiveness near sensitive borders, foreshadowing the more serious 2020 Galwan clash.

events.title: Balakot airstrike and Article 370 revocation
events.what_happened: Following the Pulwama suicide bombing (Feb 2019) that killed 40 Indian paramilitary personnel, India conducted airstrikes on an alleged militant camp in Balakot, Pakistan. Later that year, India revoked Jammu & Kashmir's special constitutional status (Article 370) and reorganised it into two union territories.
events.why_it_happened: The Balakot strike was a response to the Pulwama attack, which India attributed to a Pakistan-based militant group. The Article 370 revocation reflected the BJP government's longstanding political commitment to fuller integration of J&K.
events.consequences: Balakot marked the first use of airpower across the international border between the two nuclear-armed neighbours since 1971; Article 370's revocation triggered a security lockdown in J&K and sharp criticism from Pakistan.
events.long_term_significance: Raised the baseline severity of India-Pakistan military responses and reshaped the legal/political status of Jammu & Kashmir.

events.title: Galwan Valley clash
events.what_happened: Indian and Chinese troops engaged in violent hand-to-hand clashes in the Galwan Valley along the Line of Actual Control, resulting in the first fatalities on the India-China border in over 40 years.
events.why_it_happened: Competing infrastructure buildup and patrolling disputes along the poorly demarcated LAC in eastern Ladakh.
events.consequences: Both sides suffered military casualties; large-scale troop and infrastructure buildup followed on both sides of the LAC, which continues today.
events.long_term_significance: Marked the most serious India-China military crisis since 1962 and hardened India's threat perception of China.

events.title: Pahalgam attack and Operation Sindoor
events.what_happened: A militant attack near Pahalgam in Indian-administered Kashmir killed 26 people on 22 April 2025. India launched 'Operation Sindoor' on 7 May 2025, striking targets inside Pakistan; four days of strikes and counter-strikes followed before a ceasefire was announced on 10 May 2025.
events.why_it_happened: India attributed the Pahalgam attack to Pakistan-based militants and retaliated militarily; both sides then exchanged strikes before international pressure and direct military-to-military contact led to a ceasefire.
events.consequences: India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty; the ceasefire has broadly held despite mutual accusations of violations; reporting since (including an Aug 2026 China-Turkey arms airlift to Pakistan) suggests continued regional realignment.
events.long_term_significance: The most serious India-Pakistan military crisis since Kargil, and the reason the Indus Waters Treaty — previously untouched even during past wars — is now suspended.
